findings.text: The network driver advertises itself as a virtio driver bound to the network device identifier with any sub identifier, exposing probe remove validate and configuration change handlers plus optional suspend freeze and resume restore handlers, and publishes separate modern and legacy feature tables whose sizes are derived from the tables themselves.

Module entry establishes two processor hotplug states for online handling and dead handling before registering the virtio network driver, unwinding previously established states when a later step fails, while module exit unregisters the driver and then removes both hotplug states in reverse order.

Probe completion turns the carrier off first, then when the status feature is present triggers a configuration change to learn link state, otherwise records link up locally refreshes settings and turns carrier on, and only after releasing the networking lock registers processor notification with failure leading to full device teardown.

Probe failure after device creation follows a fixed unwind order of unregistering the network device, destroying failover support, destroying page pools, freeing interrupt moderation, resetting the virtio device, deleting queues, and finally freeing the network device structure before returning the error.

Common queue teardown resets the device, releases unused and receive buffers, resets transmit queues, destroys page pools and deletes queues. Remove additionally stops processor notification, flushes configuration and receive mode work, frees moderation, unregisters the device and destroys failover before common teardown. Freeze stops notification, downs the device and then runs common teardown. Restore brings the device up, restores queue count and readds notification, rolling back to down plus common teardown when notification registration fails.

The base feature set covers checksum, segmentation, mergeable receive, status, control queue and related offload capabilities. The modern table extends the base with guest and host UDP tunnel segmentation variants including checksum variants, while the legacy table extends the base with generic segmentation and any layout support.

Configuration change notification is serialized by acquiring the device configuration lock with interrupts saved, invoking the internal change helper, and then releasing the lock with interrupts restored.

Device configuration reads may sleep. Multi element reads sample an optional generation counter before and after fetching each element through the transport get operation and repeat until the generation is stable. Single byte reads perform one transport get. Single thirty two bit reads perform one transport get followed by endian conversion to host order. Byte array reads use the multi element path with single byte elements.
The hypervisor console driver uses major number two hundred twenty nine and minor number zero.
Close drain wait is one tenth of a second, expressed as the system tick rate divided by one hundred.
Console chunk sizes for output and input are sixteen each, atomic read maximum is one hundred twenty eight, and poll outcome flags use value one for read need and value two for write need.
Poll backoff starts at ten milliseconds and grows toward two thousand milliseconds. The console layer supports sixteen console instances and preallocates space for eight terminal adapters.

Debug communication channel status uses bit thirty for receive readiness and bit twenty nine for transmit readiness, with input buffering of one hundred twenty eight bytes and output buffering of one thousand twenty four bytes.

Each console instance anchors on a terminal port, adds a private spin lock, an index, wakeup and sizing state for pending output, a terminal number, a pointer to backend operations, interrupt and private data fields, a cached window size with deferred resize work, list linkage, flags, and a trailing word aligned flexible output area.

Backend operations group character transfer handlers for fetch and store, an optional flush with wait control, lifecycle notifiers for add remove and hangup, modem line get and set handlers, and a data terminal ready plus request to send control handler, where several handlers are optional and checked before use.

A global mutex guards the list of console instances and is held while walking or unlinking entries. Lookup additionally takes each instance lock with interrupts saved to compare the index safely. Destruction holds the global mutex while taking the instance lock to unlink, then releases both before freeing the instance.
Open count changes are protected by the port lock with interrupts saved. Output staging and window size snapshots are protected by the instance lock with interrupts saved.
A dedicated spin lock object is defined for the debug communication channel, with no use sites visible in these fragments.

Lookup by index walks the global list under the global mutex, checks each index under that instance lock, and on match acquires a terminal port reference that keeps the instance alive before releasing locks and returning it, otherwise reports absence when no index matches.
Flush helpers invoke the backend flush when present and report success otherwise. The console path never waits and never sleeps for that reason, while the terminal path always waits and may sleep.

Kernel console output ignores writes with an out of range index or with a removed adapter marker, expands each newline with a preceding carriage return, emits in small aligned chunks through the per index backend, retries with a flush when the backend reports try again, discards the chunk on other errors, compacts any partial progress, and flushes once at the end.

The kernel console descriptor is named hvc, wires write device and setup handlers, requests buffered print replay, and starts with an invalid index. Registration happens at early init. Device returns no driver for removed adapters, setup reports device absence for out of range indexes and removed adapters, otherwise the console index is bound to the terminal driver.

Instantiation validates that the index is in range and its slot is still marked removed and that no terminal instance already uses the index, then records the terminal number and backend operations for that slot and rechecks console binding, returning negative one for any validation error.

First open binds the terminal, attempts backend notifier registration, raises data terminal ready when a baud rate is configured, marks the port initialized and kicks polling even on failure. Concurrent opens only bump the count and kick. Final close clears the terminal pointer, and when initialized lowers data terminal ready when hangup on close is set, removes the notifier, cancels resize work, waits for drain bounded by the close wait, and clears initialized. A negative count is reported as an error.

Install resolves the instance by terminal index and reports a device absence failure when missing, otherwise stores it as driver data and installs the port, dropping the acquired reference on install failure. Cleanup drops that reference. Hangup cancels resize work, ignores calls when no opens remain, otherwise zeroes the count, clears the terminal pointer, resets pending output length and invokes the backend hangup notifier when present.

Write reports a pipe failure when driver data is missing and an input output failure when the port shows no opens, otherwise stages caller bytes into free tail space under the instance lock, pushes pending output, flushes and yields when more input remains, and kicks the background thread before reporting staged bytes. Room reports free tail space and buffered count reports filled tail space, each reporting zero when driver data is missing.

Deferred window size handling obtains a terminal reference and returns silently when none exists, otherwise snapshots the cached size under the instance lock, applies it to the terminal, and releases the reference.

The background thread is freezable and its identity is kept in a global task pointer, clears a global kick flag each round, polls every instance under the global mutex unless processors are in the debugger in which case it records read need, restarts immediately when kicked, sleeps until kicked when no work remains, and otherwise sleeps interruptibly with a backoff that grows additively from the minimum toward the maximum, using distinct read and write need flags for poll outcomes.

The terminal operations table wires install open close cleanup write hangup unthrottle room buffered count and modem line handlers, with additional poll handlers available when console polling is configured. The port operations table wires only the destruct handler.

Modem line get and set delegate to the backend and report an invalid argument failure when instance or backend handler is missing. Poll initialization always succeeds. Poll fetch reads one byte from the first terminal backend and maps empty or error to a no character sentinel. Poll store spins on the backend until one byte is accepted. Unthrottle only kicks the background thread.

The open count guard in the write path is read without holding the port lock, so a racing close or hangup can change the outcome after the check, a risk already flagged by a fixme note in the fragment.

Console output spins with flush retries while the backend reports try again and silently drops buffered characters on other errors, which can delay progress under a stuck backend or lose messages on persistent failure.
Room and buffered count queries read size fields without acquiring the instance lock, so concurrent writes that stage bytes under the lock can make the reported values stale or inconsistent.

Per console backend pointers and terminal numbers are held in fixed arrays sized by the maximum console count, with every terminal number initially marked removed so early console calls safely no op until instantiation records a real backend.

Global console state includes a kick flag for waking the background thread, a system request key flag, a last allocated index starting at negative one, and an initialization need counter starting at negative one held in mostly read memory.
The layer keeps a global terminal driver pointer and a global background task pointer.
The shared console header is protected by a conventional include guard macro.
